newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Gov't confirms Brazil coffee council to meet Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: Gov't confirms Brazil coffee council to meet Feb 4.

text.p: A new Brazilian coffee council joining the public and private sector will meet informally in Brasilia on February 4, a spokesman for the National Coffee Department confirmed on Friday.
"It will be an informal meeting," said Roberto Abreu. "The private sector is coming for preliminary contacts. I don't know if everybody will take part."

The Conselho Deliberativo da Politica do Cafe (CDPC) or Deliberative Council for Coffee Policy is due to hold its official inaugural meeting in Vitoria on March 3. The date of the first meeting has been repeatedly postponed.
The CDPC is made up of six representatives each from the private and the public sector and will be presided over by Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles.
Luis Hafers, vice-president of the National Coffee Council, on Thursday said an earlier informal meeting would take place on February 4.
It was likely to discuss the possibility of the government raising the limit on its monthly coffee stock auctions, he said.
